lines: - **question-needs-design** A question of what people want or what is good: look for a ready answer, else pick a design sprint or the five modes.
- **open-a-design** Open a design for a design sprint and start with Empathize on the PO's permission, never with solutions; a blank page is one.
note: The pointers become handles: sprint-or-modes, stage-gates and blank-page. Line 1 is over the soft limit on purpose; it keeps the 'ready answer first' test.

line: - **hard-point-only** From a Sprint, take out only the hard point that needs design; the rest of the Sprint goes on.

lines: - **design-roles** [po,sm,des] The PO and Scrum Master settle Empathize and Define; the Designer takes over at Ideate. Read details/design.md first.
- **one-session-both-roles** [po,sm,des] A design often needs one session; the PO decides if it plays both roles; its name goes in both header fields.
note: The old rule also pointed at the list of what the PO decides (design-log#21); that list is the stage-gates and design-stage lines. The loss lens found the 'same name in both fields' sentence only here, so it stays in a line.

line: - **design-branch** A design opens its own branch off the Sprint branch or main; never name it <sprint-branch>/<name> (git cannot hold a and a/b).
- **design-folder** A design lives in scrum/design-<suffix>/ (suffix: subject, no number); prototypes and working material never go into an Increment.
- **design-stages** Each design stage: people first, experts if unclear, the map, ideas, prototype, role-card test. Read details/design.md first.
note: The index line for the stage details. design-log#6: start Empathize with the people concerned; when the PO is the person concerned ask first for concrete experiences, then for their call on what it means, otherwise start with users the PO can bring; documents and role cards come after; mark each finding first-hand or second-hand; write the design goal as a vision, not a how; keep the one-row commitment table in 1.2.

After hearing the people, write the challenge, the design goal and the design questions; ask experts (the PO in the conversation, role cards each played by a fresh subagent) and do research only if still unclear; draft a rough map first; the log keeps what changed, not each interview; afterwards refine all three and redraw the map.

Map: a Mermaid flowchart TD, actors at the top and the ending at the bottom, rough (five or six boxes, one loop), the experience we want not today's (today's goes in chapter 1 with sources; departs from the book); branches, exceptions and solutions are not in the map (a reader who never learned design who cannot read it at a glance means a solution is inside); the map with the challenge, goal and questions is the point of view; the PO picks the How Might We questions, no dot voting; no target step while the design runs; a blank-page design picks its target when it ends; split a map that holds more than one design's work.

Lightning Demos is optional: when existing ideas would help, have subagents search for them in parallel and keep the list as working material, not in the log; if subagents sketch, split the list among them so each starts from different ideas.

line: - **diverge-first** Sketchers diverge first: two methods, one an ideo-kernel Ideate method, quantity, no judgment. Read details/design.md first.
note: The sentence 'when you brief a subagent, tell it so' and 'the ideas are working material and stay out of the log' are in the design-stages long file (section Ideate: diverge before you converge).

Isolated solutions (optional, Decide on the spot): several fresh subagents that cannot see one another each sketch one complete solution in words or Mermaid, each with its own materials (chapters 1 and 2 and its own part of the ideas, or none until it has drawn) and its own summary (one summary for all makes them converge: two subagents given the same summary both drew a subway map), nothing about how things are solved today and told not to read the project's files; each diverges first; some tools hand the project's instructions to every subagent anyway and then that is noted in the design log; without subagents the main thread and the PO sketch together. Whether to use subagents, how many and on which model is decided within how the PO chose to run this round.

line: - **talk-with-po** The main thread talks ideas over with the PO and merges all lines before converging; with none from the PO, it sketches one.
- **choose-with-po** [po,sm] The Scrum Master leads the choice, the PO decides, no consensus hunt; role-card poll if asked; only the choice in 3.1.
note: Only the chosen solution goes into 3.1 (the template has it).

line: - **combine-or-rumble** Combine winners that fit; when two conflict, prototype both and let the test decide; the PO decides which.
- **storyboard** Write a storyboard of about fifteen steps in 3.2 only when the solution needs one before the prototype; the Designer writes it.

note: Supplement. Build in the design folder from the chosen solution, real enough for honest reactions, made quickly for learning not production while the surface the tester sees appears real; keep it as design evidence, which does not make it an Increment; subagents can build parts while one session stitches; do a trial run against the solution and the design questions before testing and write what it found in chapter 5; list each part in chapter 4 with the design question it tests. Decide on the spot: how real the prototype must be when the product has no screen, agreed with the PO.

Test with role cards, each a fresh subagent given only its card, the prototype and the tasks; the PO tests too; the Designer runs the Five-Act Interview; a grid of reactions is working material; chapter 5 keeps who tested, what showed up, and the answer to each design question; test with the role cards the prototype is about, add runs while patterns are unclear (the book tests five customers); when the thing is for the PO alone, the PO testing it is enough and no role card is made up.

line: - **criteria-before-test** Before testing, write what counts as a yes, a no or a not yet for each design question, and what role cards cannot show.
